Quick summary (recommended): Efficiency Accelerator (recommended) — 60 day pilot - Includes: 100k generation tokens + 20k embedding tokens (pilot credits), 1 technical workshop (billing/quantization + batching/caching playbook), 8 hours of SE time for integration, and a quantization trial run on a representative model.
- Expected outcomes: 2–4x token cost reduction from quantization + cache/batch gains; latency impact depends on target SLOs.
- Commercial: $12,500 pilot fee offsettable by credits; we typically grant a 12% first-year discount if customer commits to a 12-month reserved capacity after pilot.

Alternative: Starter Pilot — 30 day, 25k gen tokens, 1 SE hour, $3,500 (good for early validation).

Alternative: Dedicated Preview — 90 day reserved pool (discounted commit), higher throughput SLAs, enterprise onboarding + extended observability add-on.

Quantization guidance (short):
- Recommend starting with an int8 / mixed-precision pass where compatible and a single-node 4-bit eval (GQT/GPTQ) against your most common prompt shapes.
- For multi-turn chat with prefix caching, 4-bit per-channel GPTQ usually gives ~2.5–3.5x token cost savings with minimal quality delta for retrieval-augmented prompts; int8/mixed can be a lower-risk middle ground.
- KV cache effects: quantizing aggressively may increase inference time for longer histories unless we use kernel optimizations and cache-aware decode paths; we'll validate with your 512 avg seq len.

Next steps: If you’re aligned, I’ll schedule a joint scoping call with SE (Connor) and our ML lead (Karthik) to configure the quantization and caching experiments. Connor, Karthik — are you available for a 60-minute scoping session tomorrow or Friday?

Hannah / team — quick technical notes (summarized):

Quantization:
- Recommendation: run a two-track experiment in parallel: (A) per-channel GPTQ 4-bit on a prod-like checkpoint for quality benchmarking, (B) int8/mixed-precision baseline for latency stability.
- Expected savings: 4-bit GPTQ typically 2.5–4x token compute reduction vs fp16 on our stacks; int8 closer to ~1.6–2x. Variance depends on prompt diversity and RAG temperature.
- Risks: 4-bit can expose small regressions on low-frequency tokens; require a focused eval set (we should use your triage prompt bank of ~200 prompts).

KV caching and latency:
- For avg seq len ~512, prefix caching yields biggest wins when user sessions are multi-turn (>3 turns). Cache hit ratio assumptions matter — recommend instrumenting cache hits during pilot.
- Note: aggressive quantization may increase per-token decode time for long KV sequences if kernels lack cache-aware optimizations; we'll test with your seq-length profile.

Batching:
- If your traffic patterns are bursty, configured batching window of 20–30ms with adaptive group sizes usually balances tail latency and throughput.
- For steady enterprise query rates, sustained batch sizes of 6–12 tokens/req give good GPU utilization; we can simulate with your QPS numbers.

Operational knobs to include in pilot:
- KV prefix caching enabled with 48h TTL for session tokens (configurable).
- Automatic fallback policy to int8 if 4-bit variant regresses beyond threshold on eval set.

I’ll prepare a short test plan and expected cost/savings spreadsheet for the scoping call.

—Dylan
